name: OpenEnergyMonitor EmonTx Sensors
description: The `emontx` component allows you to use ESPHome to create a connection to an OpenEnergyMonitor emonTX via a supported device (ESP32 recommended). This component is a global hub that establishes the connection to the EmonTx via [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart) and translates the received data. Using the [emontx sensors](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/emontx/#sensors), you can then create sensors for Home Assistant that track voltage, current, power as measured by CTs (up to 12), pulse data, and temperature depending on the configuration of the emonTX.

config_entries.label: UART ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the [UART Component](https://esphome.io/components/uart) if you want to use multiple UART buses.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation or multiple hubs.

config_entries.label: Lock On Reboot
config_entries.description: The ESPHome device sends `emonlock` to the EmonTx right before it reboots (OTA update, restart, safe mode, ...), and `emonunlock` once it has booted. While locked, the EmonTx ignores configuration commands, so serial noise during the reboot cannot change its settings. A crash, watchdog reset or power loss skips the lock. These commands need EmonTx firmware v1.2.0 or later: older firmware reads them as a request to enter the bootloader. Defaults to `auto`.

options.label: auto
options.description: ESPHome asks the EmonTx for its firmware version with the v command after it boots, and only sends the lock commands to firmware v1.2.0 or later. Nothing else is sent to older firmware. If no version arrives (ESPHome asks up to three times), no lock command is sent either: an EmonTx locked before the reboot then stays locked until it restarts or receives emonunlock (see emontx.send_command).
